title: Rabbi Shimon ben Levi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Kiddushin 40b, but the statement is cited in Sukkah 52a, and there it is Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish. In Chullin 57b (according to Dikdukei Soferim), Rabbi Yose ben Nehorai asked Rabbi Shimon ben Levi.

He is likewise mentioned in Tanchuma, Behar 7, Vayikra Rabbah 16:7 and Midrash Shmuel 18:4: his precious saying, “Whoever is merciful to the cruel will end by becoming cruel to the merciful” (Hyman’s proposed wording); in the Yalkut there the statement is cited in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. In Yalkut, Isaiah, remez 336: Rabbi Abba in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Levi. In the Yalkut on Shir HaShirim, remez 988: Rabbi Tachlifa of Caesarea in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Levi; Hyman proposes reading, as in Shir HaShirim Rabbah, chapter 4, on “Honeycomb,” in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.

notes.text: Hyman’s Shimon ben Levi/ben Lakish/Yehoshua alternatives and proposed correction of the maxim are retained as attributed textual claims, not globally merged identities.

The supplied Kiddushin 40b locator is preserved; the matching saying in the consulted text is at Kiddushin 30b, in Rabbi Shimon ben Levi’s name. Its parallel names Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish at Sukkah 52b, following the 52a folio boundary. This does not merge the people or independently verify Hyman’s exact Dikdukei Soferim and Yalkut readings.
